title: Complete adically formally smooth algebras admit a tangent power-series comparison map
statement: Let k be a field and A a complete Noetherian local k-algebra. If k → A is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then there is a ring map from A to the finite-variable multivariate power-series ring over the residue field of A [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] which maps the maximal ideal onto the ideal generated by the variables and whose induced map to the quotient by that ideal is surjective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EI, proof, paragraphs constructing f_1 and successive lifts

proof.text: Put T=K[[X_1,...,X_d]] and N=(X_1,...,X_d). Mathlib gives Noetherianity, locality and N-adic completeness. The variables are nonunits by their zero constant terms, hence N is contained in the maximal ideal and the Jacobson radical. N^2 is N-adically closed: the defining intersection contains N^2 and its m=2 term equals N^2.
Obtain the surjective first-order ring map g_0:A -> T/N^2, with inverse image of the image of N equal to m_A. No formal smoothness is needed for this finite construction.

Lift g_0 restricted to k to T to obtain a compatible scalar structure. In characteristic zero choose a transcendence basis over Q, use algebraicity and separability, and apply the Mathlib formally-smooth field theorem. In characteristic p use H1Cotangent vanishing over ZMod p and projectivity of the differential vector space. Discrete formal smoothness gives adic formal smoothness for source ideal zero. Apply the complete lifting theorem with I=N, J=N^2, r=t=1. Its reduction equality makes g_0 a k-algebra map for the constructed scalar structure.

Apply the complete lifting theorem to the assumed adic formal smoothness of A, with source ideal m_A and I=N, J=N^2, r=t=1. The inverse-image condition proves g(m_A) lies in the image of N. Obtain f:A -> T reducing to g and taking m_A into N.

For x in N, surjectivity gives y with g(y)=x mod N^2. The inverse-image condition gives y in m_A, so x=f(y)+(x-f(y)) lies in Ideal.map f m_A + N^2. Nakayama for the finite T-module N, using N in the Jacobson radical, gives N contained in Ideal.map f m_A. Combine with the reverse containment to prove equality.

For a representative x of a class modulo Ideal.map f m_A, first-order surjectivity gives y with f(y)=x mod N^2. Since N^2 is contained in N=Ideal.map f m_A, the classes of f(y) and x agree. This proves quotient surjectivity.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07EI, first-order comparison and complete lifting; Tag 07NJ for the existing general lifting interface

lean.statement:
theorem exists_powerSeries_comparison_of_formallySmoothAdic (k : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    (h : FormallySmoothAdic k A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)) :
    ∃ f : A →+* MvPowerSeries (Fin (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).spanFinrank)
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A),
      Ideal.map f (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) =
        Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).spanFinrank ↦
          (MvPowerSeries.X i : MvPowerSeries (Fin (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).spanFinrank)
            (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)))) ∧
      Function.Surjective ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map f (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))).comp
        f)
